note.explanation: Acid rain forms when harmful gases from burning fossil fuels mix with moisture in the air. It can harm soil, plants, aquatic life, and structures.
examples: SO₂ forms SO₃, which then reacts with water to form H₂SO₄.
Acid rain can make lakes too acidic for fish to live in.
note.checkAnswer: Acid rain can harm soil and plants, make water too acidic for aquatic animals, and damage buildings and other structures.
note.simple: Some gases mix with water in the air and fall as acidic rain. This can hurt living things and damage buildings.
note.checkQuestion: Name two effects of acid rain.
note.title: Acid Rain and its Effects
steps: Burning fossil fuels releases harmful gases, including SO₂ and NO₂.
The gases mix with moisture in the air and form acid droplets.
The droplets fall to the ground as acid rain.
Acid rain harms soil, plants, aquatic life, and structures.
note.answer: Acid rain is rain water with a pH between 4.2 and 4.4.

options: Rain water with a pH between 4.2 and 4.4
Rain water with a pH of exactly 7
Rain water with a pH above 7
mcqs.stem: According to this section, which rain water is called acid rain?
rationales: This is the pH range given for acid rain in the section.
A pH of 7 is neutral, not the stated range for acid rain.
Dissolved oxygen does not define acid rain in this section.
A pH above 7 is not within the stated acid-rain range.

mcqs.stem: Which harmful gases are named as forming acid droplets when mixed with moisture in the air?
rationales: The section names SO₂ and NO₂ as the gases that form acid droplets.
O₂ appears in an equation, but it is not one of the two harmful gases named as forming acid droplets.
N₂ and CO are not named in the section as the gases that form acid droplets.
H₂ and Cl₂ are not named in the section as the gases that form acid droplets.

mcqs.stem: According to the equations in this section, which acid is formed when SO₃ reacts with water?
rationales: The section gives SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄.
H₂SO₃ is not the product shown for SO₃ reacting with water.
HNO₃ is shown as a product of the NO₂ reaction, not the SO₃ reaction.
HNO₂ is also shown as a product of the NO₂ reaction, not the SO₃ reaction.

options: It dissolves and washes away nutrients needed by plants.
It adds all needed nutrients to the soil.
It makes soil neutral in every case.
It prevents plants from absorbing water.
mcqs.stem: How can acid rain harm soil and plants?
rationales: The section says acid rain dissolves and washes away nutrients needed by plants.
The section says nutrients are washed away, not added.
The section says acid rain makes soil more acidic, not neutral.
The section does not state that acid rain prevents plants from absorbing water.

options: They can become too acidic for aquatic animals to live in.
They become too warm for aquatic animals to live in.
They gain enough nutrients to support every aquatic animal.
mcqs.stem: What can acid rain do to lakes, rivers, ponds, and streams?
rationales: The section says water bodies can become too acidic for aquatic animals to live in.
The section describes increased acidity, not increased temperature.
The section does not say acid rain adds nutrients to water bodies.
The section does not say acid rain turns water bodies into drinking water.

options: Buildings, statues, automobiles, and other stone and metal structures
mcqs.stem: Which structures can be damaged by acid rain and dry deposition of acidic particles?
rationales: These are the types of structures named in the section.
Wooden furniture alone is not the list given in the section.
Paper and cloth are not the structures listed in the section.
Glass-only structures are not the list given in the section.

options: Acid droplets formed when gases mix with moisture in air
Pure water vapour rising from oceans
Dust particles that contain no acidic substances
mcqs.stem: What falls to the ground as acid rain, according to the section?
rationales: The section says acid droplets formed in air fall to the ground as acid rain.
Pure water vapour is not described as acid rain.
The section refers to acidic particles and droplets, not non-acidic dust alone.
Oxygen released by plants is not described as falling as acid rain.

mcqs.stem: Which substance is shown forming from SO₂ and O₂ in the first equation?
rationales: The first equation shows SO₂ and O₂ forming SO₃.
H₂SO₄ forms in the next reaction, when SO₃ reacts with water.
HNO₃ appears in the equation involving NO₂ and water.
HNO₂ appears in the equation involving NO₂ and water.

examTips: This section can be tested with a short question asking for the pH range or how acid rain forms.

For an effects question, organize your answer by soil and plants, aquatic life, and buildings or other structures.
Write the equations with correct formulae and balancing as printed in your textbook when the question asks for them.

hints: Think about the two harmful gases named in the section.
Explain what they mix with, then state what forms and falls to the ground.
yourTurn.question: How is acid rain formed?
solution: Burning fossil fuels releases harmful gases, SO₂ and NO₂, into the air.
These gases mix with moisture present in the air and form acid droplets.
The droplets fall on the ground as acid rain.
The section gives these reactions: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g); SO₃(g) + H₂O(l) → H₂SO₄(g); 2NO₂(g) + H₂O(l) → HNO₃(g) + HNO₂(g).
yourTurn.answer: Burning fossil fuels releases SO₂ and NO₂. They mix with moisture in the air to form acid droplets, which fall to the ground as acid rain.

hints: Think about the effects on land and living things in water.
Name the damage to structures as well as the effects on soil, plants, and aquatic life.
yourTurn.question: State the effects of acid rain on soil, plants, aquatic life, and human-made structures.
solution: Acid rain makes soil more acidic.
It dissolves and washes away nutrients needed by plants, and many plants cannot live or grow in acidic soil.
It can make water bodies too acidic for aquatic animals; many lakes, rivers, ponds, and streams no longer have fish.
Acid rain and dry deposition of acidic particles damage buildings, statues, automobiles, and other structures made of stone and metal.
yourTurn.answer: Acid rain makes soil more acidic and washes away nutrients needed by plants. It can damage vegetation, make water too acidic for aquatic animals, and damage buildings, statues, automobiles, and other stone and metal structures.

explain.title: What acid rain is
explain.body: “When rain water has pH between 4.2 – 4.4, it is called acid rain.” Remember this pH range.

explain.title: How acid rain forms
explain.body: Burning fossil fuels releases SO₂ and NO₂. When these gases mix with moisture in air, they form acid droplets that fall to the ground.

explain.title: Effects on soil and plants
explain.body: Acid rain makes soil more acidic and washes away nutrients plants need. It can damage vegetation, and many plants cannot grow in acidic soil.

explain.title: Effects on water and structures
explain.body: Water bodies can become too acidic for aquatic animals. Acid rain and dry acidic particles can also damage buildings, statues, automobiles, and other stone and metal structures.

mistakes: Giving the wrong pH range; the section states 4.2–4.4.
Saying that acid rain forms without mentioning moisture in the air.
Naming only one effect when the question asks about several areas.
Forgetting that dry deposition of acidic particles also damages structures.
